p: Nordic aliens come out of the contactee craze right after the Second World War. On November 20, 1952 George Adamski said he walked out into the desert near Desert Center, California and met a man from a landed scout ship. He described him as about five and a half feet tall with shoulder-length blond hair, a tan and a warm smile. The visitor (later named Orthon) told him with gestures and telepathy that he was from Venus and that his people were worried about our nuclear testing.

Adamski's book Flying Saucers Have Landed came out in 1953 and was a bestseller, and pretty soon other contactees had their own handsome, peaceful "space brothers" too. The message was almost always the same. Give up the atomic bombs before you wipe yourselves out.

Starting in 1975 a Swiss farmer named Eduard "Billy" Meier said he was meeting regularly with a woman named Semjase and others from the Pleiades star cluster. He put out hundreds of photos of their beamships over the Swiss countryside and long transcripts of their conversations.

His supporters still stand by him, but analysts have matched a lot of the ships in his photos to small models, and some of his pictures of the visitors match images from magazines and TV. Even so, Meier is the reason "Pleiadians" is the name most people know.

This isn't only an American thing. In 1957 a Brazilian farmer named Antônio Villas Boas said he was taken aboard a craft and met a woman with almost white blond hair and blue eyes (that story goes some places, I'll just say that). Here's the [Villas Boas case](/encounters/villas-boas-1957/). Contactees in Europe, especially Switzerland, Germany and Scandinavia, built up their own Nordic traditions, and contact groups today describe them all over the world.
Later abduction stories often put the Nordics and the greys together, with the tall human-looking ones running things and the greys doing the actual work. Kind of like a bad office job.

If you look at when these stories happened, the 1950s Nordics fit their time almost too well. The Day the Earth Stood Still came out in 1951, a year before Adamski's meeting, and its alien Klaatu is a calm, human-looking visitor warning Earth about its weapons. Venus was also still a place people imagined could have life on it, until the probes in the 1960s showed it's hot enough to melt lead.
Once abduction stories took over in the 60s, the little grey with the black eyes pushed the friendly blond guy out of most reports. Nordics still turn up, mostly in contactee and spiritual circles.

faq.a: They're the human-looking beings from UFO contact stories. Tall, blond, light eyes and usually friendly, and a lot of the time they're warning people about nuclear weapons or the environment. The name comes from how Scandinavian they look.

faq.q: Where are Nordic aliens supposed to come from?
faq.a: It depends on when you ask. 1950s contactees said Venus, Mars or Saturn. Since Billy Meier in the 1970s the Pleiades star cluster has been the usual answer, which is why they also get called Pleiadians.
There's no evidence they exist. The best-known contactees, George Adamski and Billy Meier included, put out photos that analysts have shown were models or fakes.

faq.q: What is the difference between Nordics and greys?
faq.a: Nordics are tall and look human and greys are short, hairless and big-eyed. Nordics go with the friendly contact stories of the 1950s and greys with the abductions from the 1960s on. We compare them in [grey aliens vs Nordic aliens](/compare/grey-aliens-vs-nordic-aliens/).
Orthon is the name for the long-haired visitor George Adamski said he met near Desert Center, California on November 20, 1952. Adamski said he came from Venus.
